dataset_identity.source_reference: UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 165 (Concrete Compressive Strength), doi 10.24432/C5PK67
dataset_identity.acquisition_note: The study materializes dataset.csv as pandas to_csv(index=False) of the ucimlrepo frame of UCI dataset 165. The file is gitignored in Atlas; the engine executes only when SHA-256 and size match. It is byte-identical to the source recorded by the Atlas native training runs, but the scientific reproduction reads only its own atlas_local_path.

compatibility_policy.rationale: The protocol depends on scikit-learn search, KFold, estimator and metric semantics and on pandas CSV parsing, stable within a minor release line. The pinned reference evidence (canonical-run.json) was produced on linux-x86_64 by a re-execution of the study's original linux-aarch64 canonical run; both are recorded. A different platform is a compatible difference whose numerical consequences are bounded by the tolerance policy.

membership.semantics: source-order-bound full-row hash plus occurrence ordinal; technical partition evidence only, not source or entity identity

definitions.mae: mean absolute error (MPa), lower is better
definitions.rmse: root mean squared error (MPa), lower is better
definitions.r2: coefficient of determination, higher is better
definitions.medae: median absolute error (MPa), lower is better
definitions.residuals: observed - predicted; standard deviation with ddof=1; absolute-error percentiles with numpy.quantile (linear)

selection.study_rule_reference: scripts/select_models.py::select_regression_candidate_model (eligible when baseline MAE - candidate MAE > eps*max(1,|baseline|); finalists with validation_mae <= best + 0.10; lexicographic minimum of (rmse, medae, cv_mae_std, -r2, model_id), equivalent to applying the breakers in order)

final_evaluation.fit_row_order: train rows then validation rows, each in source order (pandas concat, ignore_index)

group_overlap_diagnostic.excluded_columns_note: Age is not part of the mixture identity: curing age varies within a mixture.
interpretation: A repeated mixture does not prove duplicate entity identity.
The split is row-level, not grouped: the experiment measures row-level generalization.
Performance claims are scoped mainly to mixtures represented in the fitting data.
Generalization to genuinely new mixture designs is not established.
A grouped evaluation (e.g. GroupShuffleSplit/GroupKFold) would require a new, untouched experimental design.

exact_elements: dataset SHA-256, size, rows and columns
partition row counts, memberships and partition bytes
tolerance_policy.rationale: Reference values are recorded at full float precision (canonical-run.json). 1e-9 equals the study's own canonical_run verification tolerance, is eight orders of magnitude below the 0.10 MPa practical-tie tolerance and below any change of a single prediction, so no difference inside it can change a scientific conclusion; every identity, count, membership, parameter and decision is compared exactly. The study's own linux-aarch64 canonical run and its linux-x86_64 re-execution differ by at most 1.4e-14 (Ridge validation only), inside this tolerance.

historical_test_exposure.description: The seed-42/43 test partition was evaluated once by the study's original canonical run and once more by each governed from-scratch re-execution of the frozen contract (including the linux-x86_64 re-execution that produced canonical-run.json). No re-execution changed any development decision; the test partition is procedurally isolated, not unseen.

protocol_integrity.statement: Every selection decision derives from train-only CV and the validation partition; the test partition is evaluated exactly once per execution, after the final fit, and the mixture diagnostic reuses that single prediction descriptively.

study_observations.description: The study's original canonical run executed on linux-aarch64. canonical-run.json was built from a from-scratch re-execution on linux-x86_64 in the same locked environment, which reproduced the model bytes (6e6a5a97...) and every decision; its reference_verification block lists the only differences against the committed executed notebooks: Ridge validation MAE/MedAE and CV-MAE std differ in the last digits (<= 1.4e-14).

The study requires MAE improvement > eps*max(1,|baseline|) (~2.8e-15 MPa here); the contract declares strict improvement with margin 0. The two differ only for improvements below ~3e-15 MPa; the smallest observed improvement is 4.22 MPa (Ridge).

limitations: Educational shuffled row-level snapshot; no temporal, prospective or operational validity.

About three quarters of held-out rows share their mixture with fitting rows; performance claims are scoped to mixtures represented in training and generalization to new mixture designs is not established.
Unseen-mixture subsets are small (43 validation, 39 test rows), so their metrics are imprecise.
Associations, not causes: feature effects are predictive associations, not engineering design rules.
Row-level predictions and residuals are deliberately transient; only aggregate evidence is persisted.

authoring.method: Protocol declarations transcribed from the pinned study code and notebooks; every json_pointer expected value, protocol gate and pinned hash was materialized by pipeline.scientific_study_contract author from the pinned study checkout and re-checked by verify.
